The third view: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Pilgrims." This is because He mentioned the worshippers first and then said ﴿hunafa'﴾, and He placed Hajj before prayer because Hajj includes prayer and spending wealth.

The fourth view: Abu Qilabah said: The hanif is the one who believes in all the messengers and does not exclude any of them. So whoever does not believe in the best of the prophets, how can he be a hanif?

The fifth view: ﴿hunafa'﴾ means comprehensive of the whole religion, since hanifiyyah (the pure monotheistic faith) is the whole of religion. He (peace be upon him) said: "I was sent with the easy, tolerant hanifiyyah."

The sixth view: Qatadah said: it is circumcision and the prohibition of marrying forbidden relatives. That is, "circumcised, prohibiting marriage to mothers and forbidden kin." So His words ﴿hunafa'﴾ point to negation, and then He followed it with affirmation, which is His words ﴿and establish prayer﴾.

The seventh view: Abu Muslim said: its origin is from hanaf in the foot, which is the turning of the big toe away from the other toes until it faces the big toe of the other foot. So the hanif is the one who turns away from all religions toward Islam.

The eighth view: Al-Rabi' ibn Unays said: The hanif is the one who faces the qiblah in his prayer. He said this because at the takbir he says: "I have turned my face to Him who created the heavens and the earth, as a hanif." As for the discussion of establishing prayer and giving zakah, it has been mentioned many times. Then He said: ﴿And that is the upright religion﴾. On this there are several issues.

First issue: Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj said: That is the religion of the upright community. So al-Qayyimah is an adjective for an omitted noun. What is meant by al-qayyimah is either "the straight" or "the upright," and we have mentioned these two opinions in His words ﴿upright scriptures﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 3]. Al-Farra' said: This is an attribute-noun construction (idafat al-na't ila al-man'ut), like His words ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty (haqq al-yaqin)﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 95], and the ha' (in qayyimah) is for emphasis, as in His words ﴿upright scriptures﴾.

* * *

Second issue: In this verse there are subtle points.

The first: Perfection in anything is only attained when the root and the branch are both present. Some people exerted great effort in deeds without securing the foundations, namely the Jews, Christians, and Magians, for they may have exhausted themselves in acts of worship, but they did not attain the true religion. Others secured the foundations but neglected the branches, namely the Murji'ah, who said: sin does not harm alongside faith. Allah, Exalted is He, rebuked both groups in this verse, and showed that there must be knowledge and sincerity in His words ﴿sincere﴾, and action in His words ﴿and establish prayer and give zakah﴾. Then He said: all of that together is ﴿the upright religion﴾, that is, the clear, straight, and balanced religion. Just as the totality of limbs is one body, so the totality is one religion. The heart of your religion is belief, its face is prayer, and its tongue, which describes its reality, is zakah, because through speech your excellence appears, and through charity the value of your religion appears. Furthermore, the one who maintains (qayyim) is one who takes care of the interests of someone who cannot take care of his own interests. So it is as if He, Glorified is He, says: the one who secures your interests, both in this world and the next, is this whole. A parallel is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿a correct (qiyaman) religion﴾, and His words in the Qur'an: ﴿a guardian (qayyiman) to warn of severe punishment﴾, because the Qur'an is the guardian in guiding to the truth. This is supported by His (peace be upon him) words: "Whoever is in the service of Allah, Allah is in his service." And Allah Most High revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): "O world, whoever serves you, make him serve you, and whoever serves Me, serve him."

The second: Those who are excellent in their actions are like the Truth, Glorified is He, through doing good to His servants and the angels. The angels are occupied in glorifying their Creator. So goodness comes from Allah, not from the angels, and glorification and servitude come from the angels, not from Allah. Then when a person comes to the place of Resurrection, Allah will boast about them, saying: "These angels of Mine are like you; they glorified and declared La ilaha illa Allah. Rather, in some deeds they are like Me: they did good and gave charity. Then I honor you, O My angels, merely for what you have brought of worship, while you glorify Me merely for what I have done of goodness. You endured one of the two matters: they established prayer, which is worship, and gave zakah, which is goodness. You endured one of the two matters, while they endured both." Then the angels will marvel at them and direct their gaze toward them. Therefore He said: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate. [Saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured."﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 23-24]. Is this not an upright religion?

The third: Religion is like the soul. The life of religion is through knowledge. Then a knowing soul without power is like a paralyzed invalid, and a powerful soul without knowledge is insane. When knowledge and power are combined, the soul becomes complete. Likewise, prayer is for religion like knowledge, and zakah is like power. When these two come together, religion is called "upright."

The fourth, and it is the benefit of the order: Allah the Wise commanded His messenger to call them to the easiest thing, which is speech and belief, so He said: ﴿sincere﴾. Then when they responded to him, He increased it for him, so He asked them for prayer, after performing which the soul remains safe as it was. Then when they responded to him and He wanted charity from them, knowing that it was difficult for them, He said: "There is no zakah on wealth until a year passes over it." Then when He had mentioned everything, He said: ﴿And that is the upright religion﴾.

Third issue: Those who argue that faith is a term for the totality of speech, belief, and action use this verse, saying: the totality of speech, act, and deed is religion, religion is submission (Islam), and submission is faith. Therefore the totality of speech, act, and deed is faith, because He mentioned in this verse the totality of the three. Then He said: ﴿And that is the upright religion﴾, meaning that what has been mentioned is the upright religion. We say that religion is submission because of His words: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 19]. And we say that submission is faith for two reasons:

The first: If faith were other than submission, it would not be accepted by Allah, because of His words: ﴿And whoever desires other than Islam as religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 85]. But faith is accepted by Allah by consensus (ijma'), so it is the very same as submission.

The second: His words: ﴿So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. But We found not there except one house of Muslims﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 35-36]. The exception of Muslim from believer indicates that submission applies to him. Once these premises are established, it becomes clear that the totality of these three, namely speech, act, and deed, is faith. Then the view of one who says faith is a term for mere knowledge, or mere affirmation, or both together, is refuted.

The response: Why could it not be that the reference in His words ﴿That﴾ is to sincerity alone? The evidence for this is that, on this interpretation, we do not need to supply a hidden element, whereas you need to supply it, saying: the meaning is "that which has been mentioned." There is no doubt that not supplying is preferable. Granting that His words ﴿That﴾ refer to the totality of what preceded, it still indicates that this totality is the upright religion. So why do you say that this totality is religion? Because religion is other than the upright religion. The upright religion is the complete religion that is self-sufficient, and that happens only when religion is present and its effects and results are also present, which are prayer and zakah. If this totality does not exist, the upright religion is not present. But why do you say that the root of religion is not present, when the dispute arose only about it? And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 98, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally. They are the worst of creation.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, first mentioned the state of the disbelievers in His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists⦆ and then mentioned secondly the state of the believers in His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah⦆, He repeated at the end of this surah the mention of both groups, and so He began again with the state of the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved⦆. Know that He, exalted is He, mentioned two of their conditions:

The first of them: abiding forever in the fire of Hell. The second: that they are the worst of creation. Here there are questions.

The first question: Why did He mention the People of the Scripture before the polytheists? The answer has several aspects.

The first: that he, upon him be prayer and peace, used to give precedence to the right of Allah, glorified is He, over the right of his own self. Do you not see that when the people broke his front tooth he said: "O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know," and when he missed the afternoon prayer on the day of the Trench he said: "O Allah, fill their bellies and their graves with fire." So it is as if he, peace be upon him, said: the striking there was in terms of the form, and on the day of the Trench it was in terms of the practice which is the prayer. Then Allah, glorified is He, judged in his favour and said: just as you gave precedence to My right over your right, so I too give precedence to your right over My own right. Whoever leaves the prayer his whole life does not disbelieve, and whoever slanders a single hair of yours disbelieves. Having understood this, we say: the People of the Scripture did not slander Allah but rather the Messenger, whereas the polytheists slandered Allah. So when Allah, exalted is He, wished in this verse to mention the evil of their state, He began first with the more grievous attack by mentioning those who slandered Muhammad, upon him be prayer and peace, namely the People of the Scripture, and then secondly by mentioning those who slandered Him, exalted is He, namely the polytheists.

The second: that the offence of the People of the Scripture against the Messenger, peace be upon him, was greater, because the polytheists saw him as a child who grew up among them, then he rebuked their intellects and nullified their religions, and this is a grave matter. As for the People of the Scripture, they used to seek victory through his mission and acknowledged his coming, so when he came to them they denied him despite knowing him, and so their offence was more severe.

The second question: Why did He say ﴿disbelieved⦆ with the verb form, and ﴿the polytheists⦆ with the active participle? The answer: to draw attention to the fact that the People of the Scripture were not disbelievers from the outset, for they used to affirm the Torah and the Gospel and acknowledge the mission of Muhammad ﷺ; then they disbelieved in that after his mission, peace be upon him, unlike the polytheists, who were born upon the worship of idols and the denial of resurrection and the Last Day.

The third question: The polytheists used to deny the Creator, deny prophethood and deny the Resurrection, whereas the People of the Scripture affirmed all these things except that they denied the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ. So the disbelief of the People of the Scripture was lighter than the disbelief of the polytheists. If that is so, how is it permissible to equate the two groups in punishment? The answer: it is said, "a well is jahannam" when its bottom is far deep. So it is as if He, exalted is He, says: they were arrogant seeking elevation, so they went down to the lowest of the low. Then, although the two groups share in this, that does not preclude their differing in degrees of punishment. And know that the reason for the propriety of this punishment is that wrongdoing is of two kinds: wrongdoing towards one who has wronged you, and wrongdoing towards one who has done you good; and this second kind is the more heinous of the two. Good conduct too is of two kinds: good towards one who has done you good, and good towards one who has wronged you; and this is the better of the two. So Allah's kindness to these disbelievers was the greatest kind of kindness, and their wrongdoing and disbelief were the most heinous kind of wrongdoing. It is well known that punishment is proportionate to the offence: for insult there is discretionary punishment (ta'zir), for slander there is the prescribed penalty (hadd), for theft there is amputation, for adultery there is stoning, for murder there is retaliation (qisas). Indeed, insulting an equal requires discretionary punishment, and a sneering glance at the Messenger requires death. Since the offence of these disbelievers was the greatest of offences, they deserved without doubt the greatest of punishments, which is the fire of Jahannam, for it is a fire in a deep, dark, dreadful place from which there is absolutely no escape. Then it is as if someone said: suppose there is no hope of escape there, is there then hope of being brought out? He said: No, rather they will remain abiding therein. Then it is as if it was said: is there anyone whose heart is softened towards them? He said: No, rather they will blame them and curse them, for they are the worst of creation.

The fourth question: What is the reason He did not say here "abiding therein forever" (abadan), while He said concerning the people of reward: ﴿abiding therein forever⦆?

The answer has several aspects:

The first: to draw attention to the fact that His mercy is greater than His wrath.

The second: that punishments, prescribed penalties and expiations overlap, whereas the divisions of reward do not overlap.

The third: it is narrated as a report from Allah that He said: "O Dawud, make Me beloved to My creation." He said: "How shall I do that?" He said: "Mention to them the vastness of My mercy." So this is of this category.

The fifth question: What is the reading of the word al-bariyyah? The answer: Nafi' read "al-bari'ah" with a hamza, and the rest read without a hamza, and it is from "bara'a Allahu al-khalq" (Allah created the creation). The analogical form requires the hamza, but its hamza has been dropped, as in al-nabiyy, al-dhurriyyah and al-khabiyah. The hamza in it is like a return to the original form that has been abandoned in usage, just as whoever hamzes al-nabiyy does so too. Dropping the hamza in it is more preferable, although the hamza is the original form, because that has become like a discarded and abandoned thing. The hamzing of those who hamz al-barriyyah indicates the invalidity of the view of whoever says it is from "al-bara'", which means dust.

The sixth question: What is the benefit of His saying: ﴿they are the worst of creation⦆? The answer: it conveys both negation and affirmation, i.e., they and not others. Know that "the worst of creation" is a phrase whose detailed explanation is long: it is worse than thieves, because they stole from the Book of Allah the description of Muhammad ﷺ; worse than highway robbers, because they cut off the road of truth for creation; and worse than the ignorant boors, because arrogance together with knowledge becomes disbelief of obstinacy, and so it is more heinous.

Know that this is an alert that the threat against the scholars of evil is greater than the threat against anyone else.

The seventh question: Is this verse to be applied in its generality? The answer: No, rather it is restricted in two cases:

One of them: whoever among them repents and embraces Islam is excluded from the threat.

The second: some said: it is not permissible for those among the disbelievers who passed away to be included in the verse, because Pharaoh was worse than them. As for the second verse, which indicates the reward of the believers, it is general concerning those who came before and after, because they are the best of nations.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 98, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, they are the best of creation.﴾ On this verse there are several issues:

The first issue: There are several reasons for the good of placing the threat before the promise.

One: The threat is like medicine and the promise is like food. Medicine must be given first, so that once the body is cleansed it can benefit from food. A body that is not cleansed grows worse each time you feed it. This is what Buqrat (Hippocrates) said in *Kitab al-Fusul* (*Aphorisms*).

Two: Hide, after tanning, becomes fit for leather goods and for khuffs (leather socks), but before tanning it is not. Likewise, when a person falls into trial or hardship, he returns to God, but when he obtains worldly comfort he turns away, as He said: ﴿So when He delivers them safely to the land, immediately they associate others with Him.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 65]

Three: In it there is good news, as though He, may He be exalted, is saying: Since there was no escape from both matters, I concluded with the promise, which is good news from Me that I will end your affair with good. Were you not impure in an impure place, and then I brought you into this world pure? Shall I not bring you out to the Garden pure?

The second issue: Whoever holds that acts of obedience are not included in the meaning of faith (iman) argues from this verse that the righteous deeds are conjoined (ma'tuf) to faith in this verse, and the conjoined is other than that to which it is conjoined.

The third issue: He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾ and did not say "Indeed, the believers," to indicate that they established the market of Islam when it was slack, and gave up wealth and their lives for its sake. For this reason they deserved the great virtue, as He said: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest.﴾ [al-Hadid: 10] The word ﴿āmanū﴾ (they believed) means they performed faith once.

Know that those who require muwafah (the notion that one's faith must continue until death) argue from this verse, because it indicates that whoever comes with faith once has this reward, while whoever dies in disbelief does not have this reward. So we know that faith did not truly proceed from him before that.

The fourth issue: His saying ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ is a matching of plural with plural (muqabalat al-jam' bi-al-jam'), so one individual is not obligated to perform all righteous deeds. Rather, each responsible person has his share: the share of the wealthy is giving, and the share of the poor is receiving.

* * *

The fifth issue: Some have argued from this verse for the superiority of humans over angels. They said: Abu Hurayrah narrated that he, peace be upon him, said: "Do you marvel at the rank of the angels with God, may He be exalted? By the One in whose hand is my soul, the rank of the believing servant with God on the Day of Resurrection is greater than that. Recite, if you wish: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, they are the best of creation.﴾"

Know that this argument is weak, for several reasons:

One: What is narrated from Yazid al-Nahwi, that al-bariyyah (the creation) refers to the children of Adam, from al-bara', which is dust. Then the angel does not enter into it at all.

Two: His saying ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is not specific to humans; the angel enters into it.

Three: The angel has been excluded from the text by other proofs. They said: That is because virtue is either acquired or bestowed. If you look at what is bestowed, then their origin is from light, while your origin is from black, molded clay, and their dwelling is a house in which your father was not left after the sin, while your dwelling is earth, which is the dwelling of devils. Furthermore, our welfare is organized through them, our provision is in the hand of some of them, and our spirits are in the hand of some of them. Then they are the scholars and we are the learners. Then look at their great resolve: they do not incline toward trivial sins. Moreover, God, may He be exalted, only related of them the claim to divinity when He said: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed I am a god besides Him."﴾ That is, if they were to commit a sin, their resolve would reach a level that befits nothing but the claim to lordship. You, however, are always a slave of the belly and the private parts. As for worship, they are more devoted in worship than the Prophet, because God praised the Prophet for spending two-thirds of the night in worship, and He said of them: ﴿They glorify Him night and day, never tiring.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 20] And in another place: ﴿They never weary.﴾ [Fussilat: 38] The full discussion of this issue has already been given in surah al-Baqarah.

**His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿Their recompense with their Lord is Gardens of Eternity (Jannat 'Adn), beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.﴾

Know that the exegesis (tafsir) is clear, and we mention in it some subtle points (lata'if) in several issues (masa'il):

**The first issue:** Know that when the responsible person (mukallaf) reflects, he finds himself created amid trials (mihan) and calamities (afat). He was shaped from the most impure substance, in the narrowest place, until he came out crying, not out of separation, but complaining of the loneliness of confinement, so that he might be shown mercy. Like one released from prison, who is overcome by weeping so that he may be pitied. Then he was not pitied; rather, the midwife gripped him. He had not been tied in the womb. Then, after a short time, they threw him into the cradle and bound him with swaddling bands. Then, after a short while, they handed him over to a teacher who confined him in the classroom and beat him for instruction. And so it went until he reached puberty. After that, he was fastened with the nails of reason and obligation. Then the responsible person becomes bewildered, saying: "Who is doing these things to me, though no offense has come from me?" He kept contemplating until he found the Doer, and found Him to be knowing in a way unlike the knowing, and powerful in a way unlike the powerful. He realized that all of this, though its form is the form of a trial, its reality is pure generosity and mercy. So he abandoned complaint and turned to gratitude. Then it occurred to the servant to repay His beneficence with service and obedience. So he made his heart a dwelling for the sovereignty of His knowledge. It is as if the Truth said: "My servant, lodge My knowledge in your heart so that nothing removes it from there or precedes it." The servant says: "My Lord, You placed love of the breast in my heart and then removed it, and likewise love of father and mother, and love of this world and its desires, and You removed them all. As for Your love and Your knowledge, I will not remove them from my heart." Then, when knowledge and love remained in the ground of the heart, rivers and streams gushed forth from this spring. The stream that reached the eye produced reflection (i'tibar), and the one that reached the ear produced hearing the whispered prayers and glorifications of existent things. And so it is in all the limbs and organs. Then God says: "My servant, I made your heart like a Garden for Me, and I caused those rivers to flow in it, lasting and eternal. You, with your weakness and deficiency, have done this. So I am more worthy of bounty, generosity, and mercy. Garden for garden." Therefore He said: ﴿Their recompense with their Lord is Gardens of Eternity beneath which rivers flow.﴾ Indeed, it is as if the Generous, the Merciful, says: "My servant gave Me all that he possessed, and I gave him some of what is in My dominion. I am more worthy of generosity and bounty than he. Therefore I have made this part of it a perpetual and eternal gift, so that its permanence and eternity compensate for the deficiency inherent in being a part."

**The second issue:** Recompense (jaza') is a name for that which suffices. From it comes the phrase "the livestock were satisfied (ijtazat) with the moist grass instead of water." This conveys two meanings. One: He gives him abundant recompense without any shortfall. Two: He gives him what suffices, so that nothing remains in his soul except that the sought object is attained, as He said: ﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire﴾ [Fussilat 41:31].

**The second issue (again):** He said: ﴿Their recompense﴾, attributing the recompense to them. Absolute attribution (idafah) indicates ownership. How then is this reconciled with His saying: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence by His bounty﴾ [Fatir 35:35]? The answer: As for the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah), they say: If the Generous King said, "Whoever moves his finger, I will give him a thousand dinars," this is a condition and a recompense according to linguistic usage and convention, not according to intrinsic entitlement. So His saying: ﴿Their recompense﴾ suffices for the truth of this meaning. As for the Mu'tazilah, they said: Regarding His saying: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence by His bounty﴾, the word "min" ("by") denotes the starting point (ibtida' al-ghayah). The meaning is that the entitlement to these Gardens arose only because of Your prior bounty. Had You not created us, given us power and reason, removed excuses, and bestowed favors, we would not have reached this rank.

If it is said: If, in your doctrine, no one has a right over Him, what is the reason for binding Himself to such bounty? We say: Do you ask about His bounty of yesterday, when we did not exist? Or about His daily bounty during the time of obligation? Or about His bounty on the Day of Resurrection? If you ask about yesterday, it is as if He says: "I am exempt from benefiting, and the table is full of benefits. If I had not created creatures, these benefits would be wasted. Just as one who has wealth and no dependents buys slaves and concubines so that they may benefit from his property, so He, glorified be He, purchased this creation from the abode of nonexistence so that they might benefit from His dominion, as it has been related: 'The creation is the dependents of God.'" As for the daily bounty, al-Nu'man (Abu Hanifa) holds that it is obligatory to complete an act once begun, so the Most Merciful is more worthy of that. As for tomorrow, I am indebted to them by the rule of promise and information, so how would I not fulfill that?

**The fourth issue:** Regarding His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾, there are subtle points:

One: Some jurists said: If someone says, "I have nothing from so-and-so," this pertains to debts, and he may claim a deposit. If he says, "I have nothing with so-and-so," it refers to a deposit, not a debt. If he says, "I have nothing owed to me by so-and-so," it refers to both debt and deposit together. Knowing this, His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾ indicates that it is a deposit, and a deposit is a specific thing. If he says, "I owe so-and-so," it is an acknowledgment of debt, and a specific thing is more noble than debt. So His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾ indicates that it is like a specific, present, ready wealth. If it is said: A deposit is a trust and not guaranteed, whereas debt is guaranteed, and the guaranteed is better than what is not guaranteed. We reply: The guaranteed is better if loss can be conceived in it, but this is impossible with respect to God, the Exalted. Therefore we say: the deposit there is better than the guaranteed.

Two: When sedition (fitnah) befalls the city, and you place your wealth with the imam of the quarter as a deposit, you become free of worry. Here, sedition will befall the city of your body, and then you will fear that the devils will raid it. So place the deposit of your trust with Me. I will write for you a document about it that will be recited in the sanctuaries until the Day of Resurrection, which is His saying: ﴿Their recompense with their Lord﴾, until I deliver it to you when you most need it, on the plain of Resurrection.

Three: He said: ﴿with their Lord﴾, and in this is a great glad tidings. It is as if He, exalted is He, says: "I am the One who nurtured you first, when you were nonexistent, empty-handed of existence, life, reason, and power. I created you and gave you all these things. When you were nothing, I gave you these things, and I did not waste you. Do you think that if you acquire something and make it a deposit with Me, I would waste it? No indeed, this is not something that could happen."

**The fifth issue:** Regarding His saying: ﴿Their recompense with their Lord, Gardens﴾, there are two views:

One: He matched the plural with the plural, which requires matching the single with the single, as if one says to his two wives or two slaves: "If you both enter these two houses, then you are such-and-such." This is interpreted as each of them entering a separate house. It has been reported from Abu Yusuf that he would not break the oath until both of them entered both houses. The same applies if he owns these two slaves.

The proof of the first view is: ﴿They put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments﴾ [Nuh 71:7]. According to the first view, it clarifies that the recompense for each responsible person is one garden. However, the least of those gardens is like the world with all that is in it, ten times over, as has been related in a raised (marfu') report. This is supported by His saying: ﴿and a great dominion﴾ [al-Insan 76:20]. It may also be meant that each responsible person has gardens, as was related from Abu Yusuf, and the Qur'an indicates this, because He said: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [al-Rahman 55:46], then He said: ﴿And besides them are two gardens﴾ [al-Rahman 55:62], so He mentioned four for one person. The reason is that he wept out of fear of God, and that weeping came from four eyelids, two above and two below. He deserved two gardens for the two eyes, and so he obtained four gardens for pouring out weeping from four eyelids. Furthermore, He placed fear first in His saying: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾, and delayed fear in this verse, because He concluded the sura with His saying: ﴿That is for whoever fears his Lord.﴾ This indicates that fear must be lasting. Before the deed, what is present is fear of failure (khawf al-ikhtilal); after the deed, what is present is fear of defect (khawf al-khilal), since this worship is not fitting for that sacred presence.

**The sixth issue:** His saying: ﴿'Adn﴾ indicates permanence: ﴿They shall not be removed therefrom﴾ [al-Jathiyah 45:35]; ﴿And they will not be brought out of it﴾ [al-Hijr 15:48]; ﴿They will not desire any shift from it﴾ [al-Kahf 18:108]. It is said: "'Adana bi'l-makan" means he resided in the place. It has been related that the Gardens of 'Adn are the middle of Paradise. It was also said: 'Adn is from al-ma'din (mine), meaning it is the mine of bliss, security, and safety. Some said: It was named "Jannah" either from al-jinn, or from al-junun (madness), or from al-junnah (shield), or from al-janin (embryo). If it is from al-jinn, then they are distinguished by swiftness of movement, circling the world in a single hour, so it is as if He said: in bringing the responsible person to his desires it is in the utmost speed, like the movement of the jinn, while it is an abode of residence and 'Adn. If it is from al-junun, then the Garden is such that if a sane person saw it he would become like a madman, were it not that God, by His grace, keeps him steady. If it is from al-junnah, then it is because it is a protecting shield that guards you from the Fire. If it is from al-janin, then it is because the responsible person in the Garden is in the utmost comfort, and is like the embryo, which is not touched by cold or heat: ﴿They see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾ [al-Insan 76:13].

**The seventh issue:** His saying: ﴿flow (tajri)﴾ indicates that flowing water is finer than still water, and from this, gazing at flowing water increases the light of sight. Indeed, it is as if He said: "Your obedience was flowing as long as you were alive, as He said: ﴿And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you﴾ [al-Hijr 15:99]. Therefore, the rivers of My honor must be flowing forever." Then He said: ﴿beneath which﴾, indicating the absence of disturbance. This is because disturbance in a garden may come either from the lack of flowing water, so He mentioned the perpetual flow, or from drowning and excess, so He mentioned ﴿beneath which﴾. Then the alif and lam in "al-anhar" (the rivers) are for definiteness, so they refer to the rivers mentioned in the Qur'an: the river of water, milk, honey, and wine. Know that "nahr" (river) and "anhar" (rivers) imply breadth and brightness, so a small channel is not called a nahr; rather, the great one is called a nahr, as shown by His saying: ﴿And He subjected to you the ships to sail in the sea by His command, and subjected to you the rivers﴾ [Ibrahim 14:32], where He conjoined them with the sea.

**The eighth issue:** Know that when He described the Garden, He followed it with what is better than the Garden, namely, first, eternity (khulud), and second, good pleasure (ridwan). It has been related that he (peace be upon him) said: "Eternity in the Garden is better than the Garden, and God's good pleasure is better than the Garden." As for the first attribute, which is eternity, know that God described the Garden once as "Gardens of Eternity," once as "Gardens of Bliss," and once as "the Abode of Peace." These three attributes came about because you composed your faith of three things: belief, speech, and action.

As for the second attribute, which is good pleasure, know that the servant is created of body and spirit. The Garden of the body is the Garden described, and the Garden of the spirit is the good pleasure of the Lord. The human being's beginning is from the world of the body, and his end is from the world of intellect and spirit. Therefore He began with the Garden and made the end God's good pleasure. Then He placed God's good pleasure with them before His saying: ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, because the Eternal is the one who affects the originated, and the originated does not affect the Eternal.

Issue 9: He said, ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾, and did not say "the Lord is pleased with them," nor any of the other names. This is because the most awe-inspiring and majestic of the names is the word Allah, for it is the name that denotes the Essence and all the attributes together, I mean the attributes of majesty (jalal) and the attributes of bounty (ikram). Had He said "the Lord is pleased with them," that would not have conveyed the perfection of the servant's obedience, since the one who nurtures may be content with little. But the word Allah conveys the utmost majesty and awe, and in such a presence, pleasure is not attained except through complete action and perfect service. Thus His saying ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ conveys the praise of the servant's deed from this aspect.

Issue 10: The scholars differed regarding His saying ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾. Some said its meaning is: He is pleased with their deeds. Others said the intended meaning is: He is pleased in that He praises them and exalts them. He said: because being pleased with the doer is not the same as being pleased with his deed, and this is the closer view. As for His saying ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, the meaning is that they are pleased with what He rewarded them with of bliss and reward.

As for the Exalted's saying ﴿That is for one who fears his Lord﴾, there are several issues:

Issue 1: Fear within obedience is a praiseworthy state. The Exalted said: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 60]. Perhaps khashyah (awe-based dread) is stronger than khawf (fear), for He mentioned it in describing the angels, joined with ishfaq (apprehension), which is the stronger fear, saying: ﴿They are, out of awe of their Lord, apprehensive﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 27]. The discussion of khawf and khashyah is well known.

Issue 2: When this verse is combined with another verse, the whole becomes evidence for the excellence of knowledge and the scholars. This is because He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah﴾ [Fatir: 28]. So this verse indicates that the scholar is the possessor of khashyah, and this verse, namely His saying ﴿That is for one who fears his Lord﴾, indicates that the possessor of khashyah has Paradise. From the combination of the two verses it follows that Paradise is the right of the scholars.

Issue 3: Some said: this verse indicates that a person never reaches a level at which he becomes secure, by knowing that he is among the people of Paradise, and they took this verse as evidence for it. But this view is not strong, because the prophets, peace be upon them, knew that they were among the people of Paradise, and yet they were among the most fearful of God's servants, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the one among you who knows Allah best, and the one among you who fears Him most, and I am the most fearful of Him." And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best. May Allah send blessings and peace upon our master Muhammad, and upon his family and companions.
